title: The Great Escape
tagline: Put a fence in front of these men...and they'll climb it.
about: Allied prisoners in a new German camp dig three tunnels at once to break 250 men out under the guards' noses.
cue: Pour the moonshine when the camp celebrates the Fourth of July.
faces: Pour the moonshine when the camp celebrates the Fourth of July.

Flaky pork sausage rolls.How to make it500g pork sausage mince1 brown onion, grated1 carrot, grated40g fresh breadcrumbs1 tsp dried sage3 sheets of puff pastry1 egg, beaten4 tbsp HP SauceMix the mince, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs and sage with salt and pepper.Halve the pastry sheets, lay a log of filling along each and roll up, sealing with egg.Cut into short lengths, brush with egg and bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Serve hot with the brown sauce.Dirt-in-plain-sight black bean dipAshley-Pitt's dirt in plain sight. Black bean dip, garlic toasts.How to make it2 x 400g tins of black beans, drained2 garlic cloves1 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp ground cumin3 tbsp olive oil1 lemon1 baguette, sliced2 tbsp chopped parsleyBlitz the beans with 1 garlic clove, the spices, 2 tbsp oil, lemon juice and a splash of water until smooth.Brush the bread with the rest of the oil and toast until golden.Rub the toasts with the other cut garlic clove.Spoon the dip into a bowl, scatter with parsley and serve with the toasts.Hot lineEscape committee beef and barley stewBartlett plans to break out 250 men. Slow beef and barley stew with herb dumplings.How to make it1kg chuck steak, in chunks2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp olive oil2 brown onions, diced3 carrots, in chunks100g pearl barley1.3 L beef stock2 bay leaves150g self-raising flour60g cold butter, grated2 tbsp chopped parsleyToss the beef in seasoned flour and brown it in batches in the oil.Add the onions and carrots, then the barley, stock and bay leaves, and simmer covered until tender.Rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the parsley and salt, then stir in enough cold water for a soft dough.Drop spoonfuls onto the stew, cover and simmer until the dumplings are puffed.Swiss border rosti with bratwurstHilts rides for the Swiss fence. Potato rosti with bratwurst.How to make it1kg waxy potatoes60g butter8 bratwurst sausages1 brown onion, sliced4 tbsp German mustard1 cup sauerkrautPar-boil the whole potatoes for 10 minutes, cool, then grate coarsely and season.Melt half the butter in a pan, press in the potato and fry until a golden crust forms, then flip and crisp the other side with the rest of the butter.Fry the bratwurst and onion until browned.Cut the rosti into wedges and serve with the bratwurst, onion, sauerkraut and mustard.SweetsThe cooler ice cream sandwichesHilts's ball in the cooler. Vanilla between choc biscuits.How to make it125g butter, softened150g brown sugar1 egg150g plain flour40g Dutch cocoa1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda1 L vanilla ice creamBeat the butter and sugar, then beat in the egg.Mix in the flour, cocoa and bicarb, roll into 16 balls and flatten on lined trays.Bake at 180°C until just set, then cool completely.Sandwich a thick slice of ice cream between pairs of cookies and freeze until firm.DrinksFourth of July potato moonshineBartlett calls it shattering. Ice-cold vodka and apple.How to make it240ml potato vodka500ml cloudy apple juice1 lemon2 cups ice cubesFill 4 tin mugs with ice and pour 60ml vodka into each.Top with apple juice and a squeeze of lemon.Mugs of strong black teaCavendish's choir covers the digging.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
